answer: Each agent identity is tied to a stake slashed when one operator is caught running duplicate runtimes. A candidate must pass a challenge window proving uniqueness, so decoys burn before any reward unlocks. Scaling to a thousand faces needs a thousand full stakes, locked and idle, while payout per face stays capped at one share. Honest agents rent that capital once; a Sybil farmer pays it again and again, a cedar post of sunk cost at every bluff. Trust built this way loses money at scale, and the calm ocean of real operators is not flooded by clones, since fake quartz never becomes paid work.
